study_identification.title: Cortical thickness deviations as biomarker for subtyping and prognosis in pediatric brainstem tumors

study_characteristics.study_objective: To build a normative cortical thickness (CTh) model from healthy children and quantify individualized CTh deviations in pediatric brainstem tumor patients to identify subtypes and evaluate prognostic value (overall survival).

deviation_metric.supporting_text: We evaluated CTh deviations ... Eq. (1)... Z_ij refers to the CTh deviation ... Regions with |Z| > 1.96 were classified as extreme deviations...

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Spectral clustering of individual deviation maps to define subtypes; Kaplan–Meier survival analysis compared subtypes; age-adjusted statistical comparisons across clinical variables; examined correlation between number of positive CTh deviations and tumor volume (FDR-controlled in regional comparisons).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: CTh deviation patterns stratify pediatric brainstem tumor patients into two subtypes with significantly different overall survival; greater positive CTh deviations associate with larger tumor volumes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Regional normative models of CTh revealed heterogeneous deviation patterns. Spectral clustering on deviation maps yielded Subtype 1 (n=100) with widespread positive deviations and Subtype 2 (n=45) with widespread negative deviations. Kaplan–Meier analysis indicated significant survival differences between subtypes. Regions with the strongest subtype differences included prefrontal, superior frontal, temporal, supramarginal, and parietal cortices (FDR < 0.05). The number of regions showing positive deviations correlated with larger tumor volumes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Single-center patient cohort; lack of independent healthy validation dataset beyond cross-validation; potential batch residuals despite ComBat across pediatric datasets; limited reporting of demographics and QC thresholds; discrepancy in patient count between abstract and methods (124 vs 145); survival analysis available only for a subset with sufficient follow-up.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Individualized deviation mapping with GPR; pre-harmonization using ComBat (age, gender, TIV as covariates); ROI-level Brainnetome (210) parcellation via CAT12; subtype discovery via spectral clustering (scikit-learn); extreme deviations thresholded at |Z| > 1.96.
